gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ to leave the gallery by 6 p.m.
gaps.hint: have to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' takes the full infinitive with 'to': have to leave.

gaps.sentence: You ___ bring your own laptop — we will provide everything.
gaps.hint: no obligation, so needn't not mustn't
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is prohibited: needn't bring.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have seen a ghost — there is no such thing!
gaps.hint: a past claim rejected as impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' rejects a past claim as impossible: can't have seen.

gaps.sentence: You ___ wear a helmet when you ride a motorbike — it is the law.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses strong obligation, often from rules or laws: must wear.

gaps.sentence: It ___ be the postman — he has already been this morning.
gaps.hint: ruled out by what already happened
gaps.explanation: Evidence that rules something out uses 'can't': can't be.

gaps.sentence: How ___ you speak to me like that!
gaps.hint: outrage with the phrase how dare
gaps.explanation: 'How dare you' expresses outrage at someone's behavior: dare.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ leave the examination room without permission.
gaps.explanation: Formal rules use 'may not' (or 'must not') to deny permission: may not leave.

gaps.sentence: He ___ be hungry — he has just eaten a three-course meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' rules out the possibility based on evidence: can't be hungry.
